sections.heading: Ichor Math Compendium
content: A canon-ready mathematical framework for divine electrochemical fluid, fluid-electric discharge, skyship power, Thundercoil charge, healing, mutation, and industrial scaling.

Core design law: Ichor is treated as a divine bioelectrochemical suspension: part redox-flow electrolyte, part hypergolic propellant analogue, part ionic liquid, part plasma precursor, and part sacred contaminant. Every equation below is a worldbuilding model, not a real-world chemical procedure.

sections.heading: 1. Canon framing and safe use of the math
2. Measurement system, units, symbols, and source keys
3. Ichor states, grades, and engine roles
8. Conductivity, resistance, coils, and charge packs
9. Plasma sheath, arcs, and fluid-electric jets
11. Rocket, thrust, specific impulse, and skyship impulse math
12. Thermal management, cooling, and runaway containment
13. Pressure vessels, membranes, rupture, and fatigue
14. Lift, buoyancy, sail-field coupling, and skyship power
15. Thundercoil scaling from hand weapons to ship engines
16. Light, flame color, chemiluminescence, and cyan signature
17. Healing, mutation, dosage, toxicity, and divine resonance
18. Purity, contamination, corruption, and legal grading
1. Canon Framing and Safe Use of the Math
content: This compendium gives Belavadös a repeatable mathematical language for ichor. It keeps the horror intact while making the technology feel engineered: priests harvest, refiners denature, guilds certify, captains budget, mechanics maintain, smugglers contaminate, and engines obey numbers even when the numbers are haunted.

The central canon rule is separation. Ichor becomes safest when divided, diluted, bonded, cooled, grounded, and metered. It becomes dangerous when opposing fractions touch directly, when membranes tear, when catalysts overheat, when prayer resonance overloads the charge, or when living divine residue begins behaving as if it wants something.

The math below intentionally avoids real-world procedural recipes. Real chemical examples are used only as analogies: combustion explains fuel and oxidizer logic, hypergolic propellant behavior explains contact ignition, flow batteries explain separated liquid charge, fuel cells explain chemical-to-electrical conversion, plasma explains conductive luminous gas, and rocket equations explain momentum exchange. In-world materials use fictional names such as fresh ichor, black ichor powder, breath-salt, storm-brass, aether niter, saintglass membrane, godsblood brine, void char, and hunger ash.
Canonical sentence: Ichor is not lightning in a bottle; it is divine hunger forced into an electrochemical bookkeeping system.

sections.heading: 2. Measurement System, Units, Symbols, and Source Keys
content: Belavadös engineers use mundane units when building hulls, tanks, nozzles, wheels, and masts. Temple engineers add divine units for potency, resonance, purity, hunger, and corruption. A mixed system works best for play: real equations handle scale, while Belavadös coefficients bend the results toward fantasy without losing internal consistency.

sections.heading: 3. Ichor States, Grades, and Engine Roles
content: Ichor is strongest when the setting distinguishes state from grade. State says what form the substance is in. Grade says how safely civilization can use it. A drop of fresh godblood, a spoon of black powder, and a tank of denatured catalyst oil may all come from the same source, but their equations belong to different machines.

sections.heading: 4. Master Variables and Dimensional Checks
content: All ichor math should pass a simple check: units must make sense. If an equation creates energy, the result should be joules or an in-world energy unit. If it creates thrust, the result should be newtons or a force-like rating. If it creates risk, the result should be dimensionless. This lets you bend equations without breaking the world.

sections.heading: E_available = m_i * e_i * Pi * eta_reaction * eta_containment
content: Available energy equals ichor mass times usable energy density, reduced by purity, reaction efficiency, and containment losses. Use this for fuel budgeting and city-scale power.

sections.heading: P_output = E_available / t
content: Power is energy delivered per time. A tiny cell can hold large energy but still be low power if it releases slowly.

sections.heading: Risk = Severity * Probability * Exposure * Moral_Load
content: A worldbuilding risk equation. Moral_Load lets divine exploitation make legal fuel politically safer but ethically heavier.

sections.heading: Safety_Margin = Rated_Limit / Operating_Load
content: Keep this above 1.5 for civilian machines, above 2.0 for passenger skyships, and above 3.0 for temple-prison infrastructure.

sections.heading: 5. Energy Release, Potency, and Efficiency
content: Ichor energy density should not be constant. Common industrial catalyst should be weaker than fresh divine blood because it has been denatured for safety. Starved-god ichor should be powerful but unstable. Primordial ichor should produce absurd energy and apocalyptic instability. This gives engineers a reason to prefer legal fuel even when smugglers can offer stronger black-market fuel.

sections.heading: IPI = 10 * Pi * (1 + 0.6*H + 0.4*Psi) * G_s
content: A tabletop potency index. Pi is purity, H is hunger instability, Psi is resonance load, and G_s is a god-source multiplier.

sections.heading: E_burst = E_available * min(1, IPI/8) * eta_burst
content: Burst energy is the portion of stored energy that can be released quickly. High energy does not always mean high burst unless the engine can vent it.

sections.heading: 6. Separated-Reagent Reaction Kinetics
content: Belavadös engines work because separated components are stable alone and dangerous together. Instead of writing recipes, use reaction-rate math. The reaction rate rises with concentration, temperature, catalyst surface, and resonance. Safety comes from limiting contact area, limiting time, and preventing backflow.

sections.heading: rate = k_eff * [I]^a * [B]^b * A_contact
content: The reaction rate increases with ichor fraction concentration [I], breath-salt/brine concentration [B], and contact area. Use only fictional reagents.

sections.heading: k_eff = k_0 * exp(-E_a / (R*T_eff)) * (1 + C_cat + Psi - S_stab)
content: The effective rate constant rises with heat, catalyst, and resonance, and falls with stabilizers. This is the safe worldbuilding version of temperature-sensitive reaction math.

sections.heading: T_eff = T + T_arc + T_prayer + T_friction
content: The engine can overheat chemically, electrically, ritually, or mechanically.

sections.heading: 7. Redox-Flow and Fuel-Cell Behavior
content: The strongest mundane analogue for safe ichor power is the redox-flow battery: charged fluids remain in separate reservoirs and produce power as they pass through an electrochemical reactor. Belavadös adds divine resonance, living catalyst, and rune membranes. If the fluids exchange charge through a membrane, the engine works. If they mix directly, the result is fluid lightning.

sections.heading: V_cell = V_0 + K_god + K_rune - (R*T / (n*F)) * ln(Q_reaction)
content: A Belavadös Nernst-style cell voltage. V_0 is mundane electrochemical potential, K_god is divine source bonus, K_rune is inscription quality, and Q_reaction is the concentration ratio term.

sections.heading: P_cell = V_cell * I_cell * eta_electrical
content: Electrical power from an ichor cell. Use for lamps, locks, weapons, medical tools, and ship control circuits.

sections.heading: E_tank = V_tank * C_charge * V_cell * eta_storage
content: Flow-cell energy scales with tank volume and charge concentration. This makes large ships possible without giving every handheld item ship-scale output.

sections.heading: Crossover_Loss = k_membrane * Area_membrane * DeltaC * t
content: Membrane leakage over time. Old or damaged membranes slowly poison the opposite reservoir.

sections.heading: 8. Conductivity, Resistance, Coils, and Charge Packs
content: Thundercoil technology becomes consistent when a charge pack is treated like a compact ichor flow cell feeding a coil. Current creates the control effect; overcurrent creates heat, arc flash, nerve stun, pack ejection, or catastrophic coil breach.

sections.heading: R_path = L_path / (sigma_i * A_path)
content: Resistance falls when conductivity or conductor area rises. Long, thin, corroded paths overheat.

sections.heading: P_heat = I_cell^2 * R_path
content: Heat buildup in coils and conduits. This is why overloading a Thundercoil should call for corruption risk.

sections.heading: E_pack = N_charges * E_shot / eta_pack
content: Pack energy equals number of charges times energy per shot, adjusted for pack efficiency.

sections.heading: Recovery_Time = Heat_Load / Cooling_Rate
content: Use this for recharge rests, cooldown periods, and large-ship firing cycles.

sections.heading: 9. Plasma Sheath, Arcs, and Fluid-Electric Jets
content: Fluid electricity is a two-phase effect: charged droplets carry mass and momentum while the surrounding air becomes ionized enough to glow and conduct. The droplet stream behaves like a pressure jet; the plasma sheath behaves like lightning; the rune nozzle forces both to stay coherent long enough to cut, weld, thrust, or stabilize.

sections.heading: E_field = V_d / gap
content: Electric field strength rises as voltage rises or arc gap narrows. High field strength ionizes air more easily.
Jet_Cohesion = (rho_i * v_j^2 * d_nozzle) / (surface_tension + turbulence + wind_shear)
A worldbuilding ratio: high inertia and good nozzle design keep the jet coherent; turbulence and crosswind break it apart.

sections.heading: Arc_Risk = max(0, E_field / E_breakdown - Grounding_Margin)
content: Arc risk rises when electrical stress exceeds the local breakdown threshold and grounding is poor.

sections.heading: Plasma_Glow = Ionization_Fraction * m_dot * v_j * Color_Coefficient
content: The visible glow follows ionization, flow, speed, and the god/metal color signature.

sections.heading: 10. Nozzle, Pressure, and Pressure-Washer Behavior
content: At tool scale, ichor discharge resembles an extreme pressure washer because liquid mass is forced through a small aperture. At ship scale, the same principle becomes a pressure column and thrust plume. The core equations are pressure, area, flow rate, velocity, and momentum.

sections.heading: v_j = sqrt(2 * DeltaP / rho_i) * eta_nozzle
content: Ideal pressure-jet velocity from pressure difference and fluid density, reduced by nozzle losses.

sections.heading: m_dot = rho_i * A_nozzle * v_j
content: Mass flow through a nozzle. Tiny nozzles can still be violent when pressure is huge.

sections.heading: F_recoil = m_dot * v_j + (p_exit - p_air) * A_exit
content: Thrust/recoil from a liquid-plasma nozzle. This is the same skeleton as rocket thrust with a denser working fluid.

sections.heading: Cutting_Index = DeltaP * A_focus * Arc_Factor / Stand_Off_Distance
content: Tool-scale cutting power. Close focus cuts metal; wider focus pushes or stuns.

sections.heading: 11. Rocket, Thrust, Specific Impulse, and Skyship Impulse Math
content: Rocket math is useful for Belavadös engines when the ship throws mass backward, downward, or sideways. It should not be the only skyship lift model because metal galleons also use keel lattices, aetheric pressure, and ichor-thread sails. Use rocket equations for burst, climb, acceleration, recoil, and fuel budgeting; use hybrid lift equations for steady cruise.

sections.heading: F_thrust = m_dot * v_e + (p_e - p_a) * A_e
content: General rocket-like thrust: mass flow, exhaust velocity, and pressure correction.

sections.heading: I_sp = v_e / g_0
content: Specific impulse in seconds. In-world, this becomes an efficiency rating for discharge lenses and reaction throats.

sections.heading: Delta_v = v_e * ln(m_0 / m_f)
content: Use only for propellant-limited maneuvers, emergency burns, and long climbs where the ship loses significant reaction mass.

sections.heading: F_vertical_total = L_aero + L_aether + T_vertical + B_buoy - W
content: A skyship climbs when this total is positive and descends when it is negative.

sections.heading: a_vertical = F_vertical_total / m_ship
content: Acceleration follows Newton second law after all lift and weight terms are counted.

sections.heading: 12. Thermal Management, Cooling, and Runaway Containment
content: Heat is the simplest way to make the technology feel real. Every reaction and every current path produces heat. Every safe machine must remove heat faster than it accumulates. If heat accumulates, viscosity drops, reaction rate rises, membrane leakage rises, and corruption risk climbs.

sections.heading: Q_heat = E_released * (1 - eta_useful)
content: Waste heat is whatever released energy does not become useful thrust, light, electricity, lift, or work.

sections.heading: DeltaT = Q_heat / (m_coolant * c_p)
content: Temperature rise from heat added to coolant.

sections.heading: Cooling_Rate = h * A_radiator * (T_engine - T_air)
content: Convective cooling approximation. More radiator area and more temperature difference remove heat faster.

sections.heading: Runaway_Index = (Heat_Generation / Heat_Removal) * (1 + H + contamination)
content: Above 1.0, heat is building faster than it is removed. Above 1.5, passenger systems should shut down.

sections.heading: 13. Pressure Vessels, Membranes, Rupture, and Fatigue
content: Ichor machines need pressure math because fluid electricity is not purely mystical. Tanks, tubes, membranes, and reaction throats are physical objects. A pressure-safe engine room should look full of ribs, hoops, rivets, sacrificial seams, glass inspection windows, and redundant shutters.

sections.heading: sigma_hoop = P_internal * r_tank / t_wall
content: Thin-wall pressure vessel hoop stress. Larger radius and pressure increase stress; thicker walls reduce it.

sections.heading: Safety_Factor_pressure = sigma_allowable / sigma_hoop
content: Pressure safety factor. Passenger engines should have generous margins.

sections.heading: Fatigue_Damage = Sum(n_i / N_i) * (1 + corrosion + H)
content: Cycle damage from repeated pressure and thermal pulses. Divine hunger acts like a fatigue multiplier.

sections.heading: Membrane_Load = DeltaP + Charge_Gradient + Prayer_Shear
content: Saintglass membranes fail mechanically, electrically, and ritually.

sections.heading: 14. Lift, Buoyancy, Sail-Field Coupling, and Skyship Power
content: A metal galleon skyship should not hover on decorative exhaust alone. Belavadös lift is a hybrid of thrust, aetheric lattice force, aerodynamic lift, sail-field coupling, and sometimes limited buoyancy. This keeps the visuals naval and steampunk while letting the physics stay legible.

sections.heading: W = m_ship * g_B
content: Weight equals mass times local gravity. Belavadös can use Earthlike g unless a region changes it magically.

sections.heading: L_aero = 0.5 * rho_air * V^2 * S_sail * C_L
content: Lift from moving air over sails or wing-like surfaces. Works best in cruise, not at a dead hover.

sections.heading: B_buoy = rho_air * g_B * V_displaced * phi_liftgas
content: Buoyancy from displaced air or enclosed lift gas. In Belavadös, phi_liftgas may include aether-vapor enhancement.

sections.heading: L_aether = lambda_a * P_lattice / v_leak
content: Worldbuilding lift: the keel lattice converts power into upward pressure. Higher lambda_a means better runes and better ichor-thread coupling.

sections.heading: P_hover_min = W^(3/2) / sqrt(2 * rho_air * A_effective)
content: Rotor/actuator-disk inspired hover power. For skyships, A_effective is the combined belly-bell, lattice, and sail-field area.

sections.heading: 15. Thundercoil Scaling from Hand Weapons to Ship Engines
content: Thundercoils and skyship engines should feel like one technology family. A pistol is a tiny metered coil. A rifle has longer acceleration rails. A shock-bomb is a deliberately unstable pack. A ship engine is a cathedral-sized Thundercoil with redundant reservoirs, pumps, nozzles, discharge lenses, cooling loops, and grounding halos.

sections.heading: P_total = Sum(P_cell_i) * eta_sync
content: Multiple cells combine only as well as their synchronization and grounding allow.

sections.heading: Breach_Radius = k_breach * (E_burst)^(1/3)
content: Blast radius scales sublinearly with burst energy. This keeps large engines terrifying without making every failure world-ending.

sections.heading: 16. Light, Flame Color, Chemiluminescence, and Cyan Signature
content: Belavadös cyan is not ordinary blue paint. It is the visual signature of ionized ichor salts, storm-brass catalysis, and divine charge release. Other gods and grades can shift flame color without changing the basic engine family.

sections.heading: Photon_Energy = h * c / wavelength
content: Shorter wavelengths carry higher photon energy. Use this as the logic behind different flame colors.

sections.heading: Glow_Output = Chem_Energy * Phi_light * eta_visibility
content: Cold-light output depends on chemical energy, quantum-like light yield, and optical clarity.

sections.heading: 17. Healing, Mutation, Dosage, Toxicity, and Divine Resonance
content: Healing and mutation should use dose math rather than simple morality. Small controlled doses can trigger repair. Medium impure doses intoxicate, distort, or addict. High doses overwhelm identity. Repeated exposure accumulates spiritual load even when the body survives.

sections.heading: Dose = mass_absorbed / body_mass
content: Basic dose scaling. Larger creatures need more substance for the same concentration, but divine resonance can override size.

sections.heading: Healing_Effect = Dose * Pi * G_heal * eta_body - Toxicity
content: Healing rises with dose and purity but falls when toxicity outruns repair.

sections.heading: Mutation_Risk = Dose^n * H * (1 - Stabilization) * Exposure_Count
content: Mutation risk climbs nonlinearly with dose, hunger instability, poor stabilization, and repeated exposure.

sections.heading: Addiction_Load = Sum(Dose_i * Euphoria_Factor * Memory_Imprint)
content: Track this for political horror: miracles can create dependency even when they work.

sections.heading: 18. Purity, Contamination, Corruption, and Legal Grading
content: Purity is not the same as safety. Legal skyship fuel is usually less pure than fresh ichor because it has been diluted and bound. Black-market fuel often advertises purity while hiding unstable hunger ash, cult residue, stolen hospital ichor, or counterfeit brine.
Effective_Purity = Pi_true - contamination - hunger_ash - water - counterfeit_salt
Inspection guilds care about effective purity, not seller claims.
Corruption_Chance = Base + 0.25*H + 0.2*Psi + 0.2*contamination + 0.15*overload - maintenance
A tabletop probability score. Convert to a d20 or d100 threshold as desired.

sections.heading: Legal_Risk = Scarcity * Purity * Source_Crime * Political_Attention
content: A smuggler equation for how badly authorities will respond.

sections.heading: 19. God-Specific Ichor Coefficients
content: God-source coefficients let ichor feel tied to the pantheon without creating twenty-two separate rulebooks. Each god modifies one or two parameters: energy density, conductivity, healing, mutation, stability, color, or resonance. Engineers care because the source changes the math; priests care because the source changes the sin.

sections.heading: 20. Worked Examples and Worksheets
content: These examples use fictional values. They are meant to help you keep scale consistent from scene to scene. Replace numbers freely when the story needs a vessel to be humble, noble, military, cursed, ancient, or experimental.

sections.heading: m_i = 0.05 kg, e_i = 0.5 MJ/kg, eta = 0.20
content: A tiny safe lantern brine cell.

sections.heading: E_available = 0.05 * 0.5 MJ/kg * 0.20 = 0.005 MJ = 5,000 J
content: Enough for low light or a short bright pulse, not a weapon.

sections.heading: 10 shots * 2,000 J/shot = 20,000 J useful output
content: A practical pack can stun or control without being artillery.

sections.heading: If eta_pack = 0.4, stored energy = 20,000 / 0.4 = 50,000 J
content: Heat and losses explain cooldowns and corruption rolls.

sections.heading: Required upward force reserve = 0.15 * W
content: A 15 percent emergency reserve gives a heavy ship enough climb margin after cargo shifts.

sections.heading: P_required = F_vertical * v_climb / eta_lift
content: The engine must spend power both to hold weight and to climb.

sections.heading: 20.4 Breach Risk Check
content: Corruption_Chance = 0.05 + 0.25H + 0.20Psi + 0.20contamination + 0.15overload - maintenance
Convert decimal to percentage. If H = 0.4, Psi = 0.2, contamination = 0.1, overload = 1, maintenance = 0.1, risk = 24 percent.

sections.heading: 21. D&D 5e-Style Conversion Notes
content: The equations should not slow down play. Use them behind the screen to decide whether a device is safe, unstable, expensive, or spectacular. In combat, convert the math into charge counts, DCs, damage dice, conditions, cooldowns, and corruption rolls.

sections.heading: Source Register and Citation Key
content: This compendium uses bracketed source keys in tables and formulas so the worldbuilding text stays readable. The sources are listed here rather than crowded into every paragraph.

sections.heading: Supplemental Mathematical Annexes
content: These annexes expand the compendium into reusable design tables. They are meant for writing, game design, engineering-flavored lore, and consistent scaling across lanterns, Thundercoils, skyships, prison refineries, portals, hospitals, and city infrastructure.

sections.heading: Annex B. Ichor Device Design Worksheet
content: Use this worksheet whenever a new ichor item, machine, or engine enters the setting. It keeps invented objects consistent with the core chemistry and physics logic.

sections.heading: Annex C. Refineries, Yield, and Denaturing Math
content: Refining turns living divine fluid into something industry can meter. The refinery never simply maximizes purity. It seeks stable yield: enough potency to be useful, enough denaturing to be legal, and enough filtration to keep engines from hearing the god too clearly.
Yield_refined = m_raw * Recovery_Rate * (1 - Spoilage - Ritual_Tax - Security_Loss)
How much usable catalyst/brine remains after legal harvesting, transport, filtering, temple claims, and black-market leakage.
Stability_Index = Denaturing + Filtration + Binding_Oil + Storage_Coolness - Freshness - Hunger - Contamination
Positive values mean the batch behaves like industrial material. Negative values mean the batch behaves like a living omen.

sections.heading: Price = Base * IPI * Scarcity * Legal_Risk / Stability_Index
content: More power, scarcity, and legal danger raise price; stability lowers maintenance cost.

sections.heading: Annex E. Thundercoil Numerical Pack
content: For play, keep Thundercoil math behind the curtain. A charge pack needs only four numbers: useful energy per shot, safe current, heat debt per shot, and breach threshold. All other drama can be generated from those.

sections.heading: E_shot = Damage_Tier * Control_Tier * Focus_Factor * 500 J-equivalent
content: A fictional conversion that scales damage and control without claiming real weapon energy.

sections.heading: Heat_Debt_per_Shot = E_shot * (1 - eta_coil) + I^2*R*t_pulse
content: Heat debt explains why repeated shots, wet weather, and overload cause failures.

sections.heading: Safe_Shots_Before_Cooldown = Heat_Capacity / Heat_Debt_per_Shot
content: Use this to decide charge count or cooldown frequency.

sections.heading: Overload_Multiplier = P_requested / P_safe
content: At 1.0 the weapon is operating at rating. At 1.5 it should complain. At 2.0 it should become a story problem.

sections.heading: Annex F. Skyship Ichor Use from the Fuel Master Perspective
content: The fuel master does not think like a pilot. They think in tanks, purity, thermal debt, membrane health, and how much of the god is still listening. Their equations turn a dramatic skyship scene into an operational ledger.
Daily_Fuel_Burn = (P_cruise*t_cruise + P_hover*t_hover + P_hotel*t_day) / (e_i*Pi*eta_reaction)
Daily fuel demand for route planning.
Emergency_Reserve = 0.25*Daily_Fuel_Burn + Storm_Allowance + Cargo_Shift_Allowance
Reserve should include weather, docking delays, and cargo surprises.

sections.heading: Tank_Segregation_Index = Number_of_Independent_Tanks / Critical_Fractions
content: A ship is safer when one tank breach cannot mix every dangerous component.

sections.heading: Field_Blackout_Time = E_backup / P_essential
content: How long a ship can keep lift, lights, steering, and medical wards alive after main reactor failure.

sections.heading: Annex G. Medical and Mutation Calibration
content: Medical ichor is a regulated poison that happens to heal at the right dose. The same equation can save a patient, addict a noble, mutate a soldier, or expose a hospital smuggling ring.

sections.heading: Therapeutic_Window = Effective_Healing_Dose / Toxic_Dose
content: Wide windows are safe medicine. Narrow windows require expert healers and monitoring.

sections.heading: Identity_Shear = Dose * H * Psi * Dream_Exposure / Will_Anchor
content: A roleplay metric for whether the patient remains fully themselves after divine healing.

sections.heading: Regeneration_Rate = k_body * Dose * Pi * G_heal - Scar_Tissue - Curse_Load
content: Use for long-term recovery, scars, missing tissue, or divine strings attached.

sections.heading: Annex H. Portal, Rail, and City Grid Math
content: Ichor should not power only vehicles. The same math supports rail wards, city lights, hospital beds, locks, messenger systems, portal gates, factories, and divine prisons. The difference is release rate and risk tolerance.

sections.heading: Grid_Load = Sum(P_homes + P_industry + P_wards + P_transit + P_emergency)
content: A city grid is a sum of loads, not a single magical battery.

sections.heading: Reserve_Fraction = (P_capacity - Grid_Load) / Grid_Load
content: Cities with low reserve fraction experience brownouts, ward flicker, and political panic.

sections.heading: Line_Loss = I^2 * R_line * distance_factor
content: Long rail or ward lines lose power through resistance and require substations.
Portal_Stability = P_field * Rune_Alignment / (Mass_Transfer + Distance + Weather + Interference)
A route gate is stable only when the field power and inscriptions outrun load and disruption.

paragraphs: BELAVADÖS
Ichor Transit Systems Dossier
Portal | Skyships | Steamships | Train/Rail | Submarines
A technical operating dossier for faster ichor-powered transit across Belavadös
Contents
1. Realmwide Operating Principles and Transit Doctrine
2. Universal Ichor Propulsion Architecture
3. Shared Ichor Math Ledger
4. Cross-Mode Transit Matrix
5. Portal: Wormhole-Gate Transit with Ichor Stabilization
6. Skyships: Airborne Galleons and Skyship-Specific Calculations
7. Steamships: Ichor-Assisted Waterborne Transit
8. Train/Rail: Steam-Electric Ichor Hybrid Rail
9. Submarines: Ichor-Assisted Underwater Passenger Craft
10. Terminals, Transfers, Scheduling, and Passenger Interfaces
11. Maintenance, Inspection, and Failure Control
12. Calculation Ledgers for Dispatchers and Engineers
13. Glossary of Transit and Ichor Terms
14. Realmwide Operating Doctrine
1. Realmwide Operating Principles and Transit Doctrine

Across Belavadös, each public transit family draws from the same licensed ichor economy while preserving the mechanical identity that makes it trustworthy at the platform, pier, lock, skyport, or portal hall.
Portal use ichor-fed field power, rune alignment, saintglass membranes, and destination-lock stability to hold a traversable throat open long enough for controlled crossings.
Skyships use ichor pressure engines, aetheric lift lattices, sail-field coupling, distributed nozzle vectors, and individual vessel calculations for lift, cruise, fuel, docking, and ground mode.

Steamships retain marine steam logic: boiler heat, steam expansion, shaft power, paddles or screw propellers, condensers, stability, and docking. Ichor makes the cycle hotter, cleaner, faster, and more compact when properly contained.

Train/rail retains rail mechanics: adhesion, traction motors, grades, rolling resistance, braking, signaling, stations, and regenerative recovery. Ichor acts as heat source, electric source, stabilizer, and route-speed multiplier.

Submarines retain buoyancy, trim, pressure hulls, life support, hydrodynamic drag, propulsors, and docking locks. Ichor powers pressure-safe propulsion, ballast pumps, quiet cruise cells, and emergency surfacing systems.

The first realmwide operating law is controlled separation. Ichor fractions and aetheric reagents remain isolated until the engine, gate, cell, lattice, boiler throat, traction stack, or pressure plant meters them through a protected exchange surface. Safe transit systems do not rely on uncontrolled mixing. They rely on valves, membranes, sensors, cooling loops, grounding plates, flow governors, and trained crew.

The second realmwide operating law is that faster transit is never free. Ichor can multiply power density, reduce route time, and let machines exceed ordinary steam-era performance, but it adds inspection requirements, thermal debt, membrane wear, contamination risk, grounding time, and legal handling burdens. A mode may be fast in motion while still slow at the terminal because boarding, stabilization, checks, and cooldown matter.

The third realmwide operating law is that each mode keeps its own identity. A steamship remains a steamship, a train remains a train, a submarine remains a pressure craft, a skyship remains a flying metal galleon, and a portal remains a spatial threshold. Ichor strengthens the energy path; it does not erase the nature of the machine.
1.1 How “ichor propulsion” differs by mode

All five transit families use ichor, but not in the same mechanical way. Belavadös engineers avoid single-purpose miracle machinery because every route problem has its own physics: portals hold geometry, skyships carry lift, steamships fight water drag, trains manage adhesion, and submarines survive pressure.
2. Universal Ichor Propulsion Architecture

A Belavadös transit engine is not a single glowing battery. It is a staged energy-conversion chain. The visible cyan light is only the final sign that a much larger bookkeeping process is happening inside tanks, membranes, channels, shafts, valves, field lattices, and station infrastructure.
2.1 Shared energy chain
1. Storage: refined ichor or ichor-derived fractions are kept in sealed tanks, cells, cisterns, or cartridge-safe transit reservoirs.
2. Separation: positive and negative fractions, conductive brine, catalyst oil, stabilizer, coolant, and grounding paths remain isolated until commanded.
3. Metering: pumps, gravity locks, feed screws, rune valves, governor plates, or pressure needles regulate flow rate.
4. Exchange: charge, heat, pressure, or resonance crosses a membrane, reaction throat, boiler jacket, traction stack, lattice ring, or portal frame without uncontrolled bulk mixing.
5. Conversion: the system turns stored potential into shaft power, traction electricity, pressure jets, lift fields, steam, propulsor thrust, or portal stability.
6. Rejection: waste heat, residue, excess charge, and contamination are removed through condensers, cooling loops, grounding rails, hull wash, purge tanks, or station dwell time.
7. Certification: public transit vehicles operate only when reserve, purity, membrane health, grounding margin, and heat removal remain inside the civilian-safe band.
2.2 Ichor states and transit roles
2.3 Shared transit engine components
2.4 Legal grades and transit performance

Legal transit fuel is not chosen because it is the strongest; it is chosen because it is predictable. A slightly weaker catalyst that behaves the same way every day is better for public routes than a more potent fuel that changes with weather, stress, contamination, or emotional resonance in a crowded terminal.
3. Shared Ichor Math Ledger

The equations below create a single mathematical language across all modes. They keep power, speed, risk, and maintenance consistent across the realm so engineers, dispatchers, and guild clerks can estimate route values before final station certification.
3.1 Core symbols
3.2 Universal equations
3.3 Route fuel budget workflow
1. Choose route profile: distance, expected speed, dwell time, grade/depth/altitude/weather, passenger load, cargo load, and terminal type.
2. Calculate motion resistance: drag for ships/submarines/skyships, rolling and grade resistance for rail, or field load for portals.
3. Add hotel loads: lighting, heat, doors, pumps, wards, life support, kitchens, communications, signage, and accessibility lifts.
4. Add stabilization loads: skyship lattice, portal field, submarine trim, marine stabilizers, rail signals, or station buffers.
5. Compute P_route = P_motion + P_hotel + P_stabilization.
6. Compute E_route = P_route * t_route, then subtract recovered energy where applicable.
7. Compute m_fuel = E_route / (e_i * Pi * eta_total).
8. Check Safety_Margin, Runaway_Index, Membrane_Load, Grounding_Margin, and reserve fuel before declaring the route passenger-ready.
3.4 Speed improvement without erasing transit constraints

Ichor propulsion makes vehicles faster by raising power density and improving control, but the setting remains believable if terminal time and safety checks remain visible. A portal may cross distance nearly instantly but require destination lock and cooldown. A skyship may outrun ordinary sailing but still need grounding and transformation corridors. A rail line may run at high speed but remain limited by curves, grades, stations, and braking distance.
4. Cross-Mode Transit Matrix

This matrix summarizes how each mode combines mechanical engineering with Belavadös ichor systems. It tells dispatch engineers which calculations matter before schedules, station records, route ledgers, or passenger alerts are issued.
4.1 Suggested operating bands for Belavadös route planning
These are planning bands rather than universal limits. They keep route timing coherent before exact route geometry, terminal class, and weather restrictions are certified.
4.2 Shared passenger information model
Route time: time in motion, or walking time through a portal throat.
Preparation time: warm-up, field lock, pressure checks, trim checks, boiler staging, traction synchronization, or sail precharge.
Boarding time: passenger loading, accessibility lift use, cargo handling, identification, and platform clearance.
Transfer time: walking distance, pressure equalization, security screening, skyport-to-ground corridor, pier-to-station link, or subterranean rail interchange.
Recovery time: cooling, grounding, purge, ballast correction, membrane inspection, or field collapse confirmation.
5. Portal: Wormhole-Gate Transit with Ichor Stabilization

Portal transit is the most tightly regulated Belavadös mode because it changes the route problem itself. A train, ship, skyship, or submarine moves through space. A portal creates a controlled threshold between two stations so passengers can cross folded distance at ordinary walking speed. The passenger experience is gentle; the infrastructure behind it is not simple.
5.1 Mechanical technology and engineering anchor

Portal engineers do not treat portal transit as a spell that makes a traveler vanish. A portal is a paired traversable throat: two mouths connected by a stabilized spatial passage. Belavadös holds that passage open through ichor-fed negative-pressure balance, rune geometry, saintglass membranes, and a controlled destination lock.

The portal face is flat enough for passengers to treat it as a doorway, but the frame behind it is a pressure machine. It must hold geometry, prevent tidal or shear effects, keep the throat clear, match atmosphere, verify the destination, and fail closed if field stability falls below threshold.
5.2 Portal architecture
5.3 Portal math
5.4 Operating sequence
1. Pre-lock: both stations exchange route authorization, staff confirmation, weather status, pressure status, and local time confirmation.
2. Membrane test: saintglass banks are energized at low current to detect leakage and contamination.
3. Coordinate braid: ring geometry and rune alignment step into the selected destination lock.
4. Field rise: ichor field power increases until the portal face becomes visible but remains physically closed.
5. Handshake: the far station verifies that its receiving hall is clear, grounded, staffed, and pressure-matched.
6. Passenger batch release: travelers cross at walking speed in counted batches with spacing between groups.
7. Soft closure: the field narrows after the final traveler clears the receiving line.
8. Cooldown: grounding halos discharge, membranes rest, heat vents purge, and inspectors confirm the face is inert.
5.5 Transit use and restrictions

Portal should be reserved for routes where the value of speed outweighs the burden of stabilization and access control. They are not ordinary casual sidewalks. They serve diplomatic corridors, emergency medical transfers, high-risk sealed cargo, restricted universities, military-adjacent dispatch, and elite scheduled crossings where identity and purpose are verified before field rise.
5.6 Example portal leg

A portal crossing from a royal capital to a mountain citadel may take only one minute of passenger walking time once the field is open. The schedule, however, should include 25 minutes of identity checks and cargo weighing, 12 minutes of pre-lock, 4 minutes of active crossing, 18 minutes of cooling and membrane recovery, and 6 minutes of station logging. The public timetable therefore lists a 65-minute controlled transfer even though the actual spatial crossing is nearly immediate.
6. Skyships: Airborne Galleons and Skyship-Specific Calculations

Skyships are metallic galleon-style vessels built from brass, copper, riveted steel, iron frames, polished defensive plates, masts, yards, ropework, cargo holds, stern galleries, service decks, and hidden transformation machinery. Their flight is not explained by a single decorative exhaust plume. A safe passenger skyship uses distributed lift: an ichor pressure engine, keel lift lattice, belly nozzles, mast conductors, ichor-thread sails, aetheric pressure fields, and controlled ground-mode hardware.
6.1 Mechanical technology anchors
Rocket and jet logic: stored energy accelerates mass through a shaped outlet, producing thrust and recoil.
VTOL logic: hovering requires upward force greater than weight and distributed control around the center of mass.
Sail and airship logic: broad surfaces can couple to wind or a field, reducing fuel load during cruise.
Plasma/electric thruster logic: charged flows can be shaped by electric or magnetic fields, while Belavadös vessels use arcane ichor-fluid discharge rather than vacuum-drive machinery.
Naval architecture: cargo belongs low, heavy machinery belongs near the keel, masts pass load into the hull, and docking gear must survive repeated transformations.
6.2 Skyship propulsion architecture
6.3 Core skyship equations
6.4 Skyship-specific personal and vessel-class calculation tiers

The skyship math should scale from personal craft to large passenger liners. A personal skiff cannot use the same heavy engine plant as a grand liner; it uses smaller cells, pulsed puffers, lighter sails, and much narrower reserve margins. A commuter galleon is the normal public-transit unit. A grand liner is slower to dock but carries large passenger loads across long regions.
6.5 Worked skyship route example

Example: a commuter sky-galleon with loaded mass of 180,000 kg operates a 300 km intercity route. Its weight is W = 180,000 * 9.81 = 1,765,800 N. With a 20% reserve, Lift_required = 2,118,960 N. If the keel lattice provides 1,000,000 N, sail-field and aerodynamic surfaces provide 520,000 N in cruise, buoyant cells provide 120,000 N, and vertical nozzles can sustain 600,000 N, then total lift is 2,240,000 N. Reserve_Lift = 2,240,000 / 1,765,800 - 1 = 0.269, or 26.9%. This is acceptable for passenger cruise, though storm operation would require extra reserve or lower cargo load.

At a cruise speed of 220 km/h, the 300 km route takes about 1.36 hours in motion before approach and terminal time. If P_cruise is estimated at 18 MW after drag, lattice, and hotel loads, then route energy is about 24.5 MWh. If legal transit catalyst provides 65 MJ/kg at Pi = 0.82 with total efficiency 0.38, fuel mass is approximately 3,000 kg for the route before reserve. A 30% fuel reserve raises planned fuel to about 3,900 kg. Route data should then add landing, transformation, grounding, boarding, and cleaning time.
6.6 Docking, ground transformation, and safety math
6.7 Passenger experience

A public skyship route should feel ceremonial and mechanical. Passengers board after the vessel has rolled through protected ground corridors and completed hull cleansing. When departing, the vessel leaves the terminal as a wheeled armored transport, clears the city boundary, deploys sails, reawakens the lift lattice, bleeds weight from the wheels, retracts ground gear, and rises in stages. This preserves the grandeur of the original skyship concept while making the sequence operationally legible.
7. Steamships: Ichor-Assisted Waterborne Transit

Steamships are the waterborne sisters of skyships: brass, copper, riveted steel, armored prows, towering stacks, reinforced boiler rooms, stabilizer arrays, gangways, paddle guards, screw propellers, and protected harbor corridors. They remain bound to water, but ichor makes their steam cycle hotter, denser, more responsive, and easier to integrate with electric auxiliaries.
7.1 Mechanical technology anchors
Rankine steam cycle: heat boils water, steam expands through a piston engine or turbine, shaft work turns a propeller or paddle, and condensers return spent steam to water.
Displacement hulls: a ship floats because it displaces water equal to its weight; hull shape controls drag, stability, and wave-making.
Propulsion: paddle wheels and screw propellers push water astern to create forward thrust; rudders redirect flow for steering.
Boiler safety: pressure vessels, relief valves, feedwater, condensers, fireboxes, and inspection schedules are the heart of safe service.
Harbor interface: piers, gangways, ropes, bollards, fenders, pilots, tides, cargo loading, and passenger stability determine dwell time.
7.2 Ichor marine implementation
7.3 Steamship equations
7.4 Faster transit without breaking marine logic

A steamship cannot simply ignore water. Hull drag, channel depth, turning radius, waves, reefs, traffic, and harbor speed limits still matter. Ichor assists by increasing shaft power, reducing warm-up time, improving condenser recovery, and smoothing the wake in certified corridors. Open-sea express ships can therefore be much faster than ordinary steam craft, while canals and crowded harbors remain slow.
7.5 Steamship operating sequence
1. Fuel and water verification: inspectors confirm ichor grade, boiler water, condenser condition, and reserve tanks.
2. Warm-up: the ichor boiler jacket raises steam pressure gradually while relief valves and temperature gauges are watched.
3. Harbor release: stabilizers and low-speed propulsors move the vessel through protected piers and channel lanes.
4. Cruise: turbines or pistons deliver shaft power; wake smoothing and condenser recovery reduce fuel burn.
5. Approach: speed drops, stabilizers hold gangway alignment, and boilers shift to maneuvering pressure.
6. Docking: hull grounding completes before gangways extend; cargo and passengers board according to trim limits.
7. Turnaround: residue wash, bilge check, condenser inspection, and pressure staging prepare the next departure.
7.6 Example steamship leg

A 90 km lake crossing at 55 km/h has 1.64 hours of movement time. If drag and propeller efficiency require 7 MW of shaft power, and hotel plus stabilizer loads add 0.8 MW, then a two-hour operating window including approach requires about 15.6 MWh before recovery. If condensers recover 10%, net route energy is 14.0 MWh. With transit catalyst at 55 MJ/kg, Pi = 0.80, and total efficiency 0.34, planned fuel is roughly 3,400 kg before reserve. The schedule still includes harbor dwell because speed in open water does not shorten gangway, cargo, or grounding procedures.
8. Train/Rail: Steam-Electric Ichor Hybrid Rail

Belavadös rail is the iron-bound land network: surface lines, elevated viaducts, underground stations, multi-line junctions, mountain tunnels, industrial spurs, and long-distance regional corridors. The system uses steam-electric ichor hybrid traction. Heat and ichor cells generate electricity; traction motors apply torque to axles; regenerative braking recovers energy; and rail infrastructure keeps high-capacity service precise.
8.1 Mechanical technology anchors
Rail guidance: steel wheels on steel rails have low rolling resistance and high capacity but depend on track geometry and maintenance.
Adhesion: traction force is limited by wheel-rail contact; too much torque slips the wheels.
Steam-electric hybrid logic: a heat source drives a generator; electric traction motors deliver controlled torque to axles.
Regenerative braking: motors act as generators during braking, sending energy into storage or route grids.
Signaling and spacing: fast trains require block control, braking distance, clear platforms, switches, and grade-separated junctions.
8.2 Ichor rail implementation
8.3 Rail equations
8.4 Rail service patterns
8.5 Faster rail through ichor

Ichor makes rail faster by giving locomotives compact high-power generation, strong electric traction, responsive braking recovery, and station grids that can support frequent departures. It does not remove rail limitations. Curves, grades, platform length, braking distance, track condition, switch speed, tunnel ventilation, and crowding still control service design.

A practical rail rule is to let ichor improve acceleration and hill climbing more than raw maximum speed. Fast passenger lines can reach high cruise speeds where tracks are built for them, while older local lines gain reliability, steadier departures, and stronger grade performance.
8.6 Example rail leg

A regional train of 420,000 kg accelerates to 160 km/h, cruises between towns, and brakes into a station. If route force averages 52,000 N at cruise, traction power at 44.4 m/s is about 2.31 MW before auxiliary loads. Add 0.45 MW for lighting, heating, doors, pumps, and signal systems. If a 75-minute run uses 2.76 MW average and recovers 12% through regenerative braking, net energy is about 3.0 MWh. With 45 MJ/kg transit catalyst, Pi = 0.78, and eta_total = 0.36, fuel mass is roughly 850 kg before reserve. Timetable design still depends on platform dwell and block spacing.
9. Submarines: Ichor-Assisted Underwater Passenger Craft

Submarines are pressure-bound transit vessels built from brass, copper, riveted steel, reinforced glass, pressure frames, ballast tanks, trim systems, propulsors, docking collars, lights, sensors, life support, and emergency reserves. They are not merely boats underwater; they are moving pressure stations. Ichor gives them quiet power, fast ballast response, long endurance, and safer station interfaces when properly governed.
9.1 Mechanical technology anchors
Buoyancy: a submarine rises, sinks, or holds depth by changing its effective density relative to displaced water.
Pressure hull: the sealed structural space protects people from water pressure and supports life systems.
Ballast and trim: main ballast controls dive/surface; trim tanks balance bow, stern, port, and starboard load.
Hydrodynamic propulsion: propellers, pump-jets, or water-moving drives push water to create thrust.
Life support: oxygen, carbon dioxide removal, humidity, heat, fire suppression, pressure control, and emergency reserves are core transit systems.
Docking locks: passenger service requires equalized pressure, sealed collars, and redundant hatch procedures.
9.2 Ichor submarine implementation
9.3 Submarine equations
9.4 Underwater passenger sequence
1. Pre-board: route water conditions, station lock pressure, passenger load, oxygen reserve, and trim baseline are confirmed.
2. Boarding: cargo and passengers are distributed to maintain center of mass and trim.
3. Seal check: hatches, docking collars, pressure doors, and emergency bulkheads are verified.
4. Initial dive: ballast tanks flood in controlled groups while trim pumps keep pitch gentle.
5. Cruise: propulsors run quietly, depth wards hold safe corridor depth, and sensors follow beacons.
6. Approach: speed drops, low-speed fins and thrusters align with the station lock.
7. Equalization: pressure and atmosphere match before doors open.
8. Turnaround: ballast, life support, residue, hull skin, and emergency reserve are inspected before the next run.
9.5 Faster underwater transit

Ichor allows faster underwater service by raising power density, reducing dependence on surfacing, and improving trim response. However, water drag rises with the square of speed and power rises roughly with speed cubed. Underwater express routes should therefore use certified corridors, smooth hulls, beacon navigation, and station locks designed for quick equalization. Speed remains more expensive underwater than in air or on rails.
9.6 Example submarine leg

A passenger submarine runs 70 km between a coastal city and a subcombined district at 55 km/h. Movement time is 1.27 hours, but pressure checks and docking locks add 50 minutes. If cruise shaft power averages 5 MW and hotel, trim, and life support average 0.9 MW, route energy is about 7.5 MWh. With 58 MJ/kg transit catalyst, Pi = 0.81, and eta_total = 0.33, planned fuel is about 1,740 kg before reserve. A separate emergency reserve must remain untouched for surfacing, lock retreat, and life support buffer.
10. Terminals, Transfers, Scheduling, and Passenger Interfaces

A unified transit system needs more than vehicles. It needs station types, transfer logic, scheduling categories, passenger alerts, accessibility rules, and consistent timing vocabulary. Ichor makes movement faster, but terminals decide whether the system feels public, usable, and safe.
10.1 Terminal types
10.2 Transfer design

Transfers should be written as actual movements, not abstract jumps. A passenger transferring from rail to skyship may need platform exit, skyport screening, ground-corridor boarding, lift checks, and takeoff. A passenger transferring from submarine to portal may need pressure equalization, dry vestibule passage, identity check, mass weighing, and portal batch assignment.
10.3 Passenger alerts and time-board fields
10.4 Timing formula
A complete transit estimate should separate motion from everything around motion:
Total_Trip_Time = Access_Time + Boarding_Time + Prep_Time + Movement_Time + Transfer_Time + Recovery_Time + Delay_Buffer

This keeps portal crossings from overwhelming station halls simply because crossing time is short, and it keeps vehicle timetables honest when the true route burden is terminal recovery rather than motion.
11. Maintenance, Inspection, and Failure Control

Ichor transit systems are only public when maintenance is treated as part of the machine. Every faster route creates heat, residue, membrane load, pressure cycling, charge buildup, structural stress, and station wear. A believable system tracks simple safety indices rather than requiring a full engineering simulation.
11.1 Universal maintenance indices
11.2 Mode-specific inspections
11.3 Failure behavior should be specific

Each failure mode belongs to its own machine family. Portal fail closed or ripple under bad alignment. Skyships lose lift reserve or develop asymmetric thrust. Steamships lose boiler efficiency or stability. Trains lose traction, braking recovery, or signal clearance. Submarines lose trim, pressure safety, or docking ability. Incidents can therefore be read by crews and passengers through visible symptoms rather than hidden mysteries.
12. Calculation Ledgers for Dispatchers and Engineers

These worksheets are intentionally compact. They can be copied into route notes, spreadsheets, JSON metadata, or station manuals. The goal is relative consistency: heavy vehicles should need more energy, rough weather should raise risk, and terminal procedures should appear in the timetable.

14. Realmwide Operating Doctrine

The realmwide transit record binds portals, skyships, steamships, train/rail, and submarines into one practical engineering language. Each family keeps its own machinery, crew practice, terminal rituals, and passenger limits, while every route draws from the same ichor ledger for power, heat, reserve, grounding, and inspection.
Civilian transit language is used throughout. Public vehicles are described by their engines, cells, lattices, boilers, gates, propulsors, membranes, and station systems.
The dossier serves captains, station masters, dispatchers, engine guilds, and table clerks who need speed, energy, safety, terminal, and passenger-facing rules in one place.
14.1 Transit Family Certification
Skyships hold full standing beside portals, steamships, train/rail, and submarines in realmwide transit planning.
Every mode carries a defined ichor propulsion or ichor stabilization role.
All five modes share a common math ledger for energy, power, purity, heat, membrane health, reserve, and route timing.
Skyships carry class scaling, personal-craft logic, passenger galleon logic, large-liner logic, lift budgets, cruise power, fuel mass, docking load, and grounding time.
Portal carry field power, mass-transfer, destination lock, cooldown, and throughput calculations for certified station use.
Steamships, rail, and submarines retain their mechanical foundations while carrying specific ichor-assisted speed and safety math.
Terminal and transfer logic treats preparation, movement, boarding, recovery, and cooldown as separate timetable fields.
14.2 Realm Continuity Checks
